sara: quick check-in: compaction on hetero hosts caused p99 blips this AM during sparse embed tests.
dave: how big?
sara: p99 ~2x for ~2m when compactor did dense move bursts. avg unaffected.
oliver: likely small-object churn + cross-node page pin overhead.
anika: what does alloc shape look like?
sara: 68% <=256B, lots of fragmented slabs.
dave: options: 1) slow the compactor (backoff), 2) implement slab-local coalesce to avoid page moves, 3) schedule maintenance compacts at night.
oliver: i prefer slab-local coalesce for small objects to avoid pin/unpin. cheap refactor.
anika: cooperative backoff sounds lower-risk short term; need metrics: compaction.moves/sec, avg_move_size, frag_pct, cpu_steal.
sara: tried cpulimit 25% -> p99 improved to ~1.1x but compaction throughput dropped 5x.
dave: so tradeoff: immediate SLO vs long-term frag. hybrid plan?
oliver: yes: adaptive backoff + nightly full compaction. adaptive uses serve_p99 and cpu_steal signals.
anika: add tenant tags to compaction telemetry so we can target heavy-tenants for maintenance.
sara: i'll open a small PR for adaptive backoff with telemetry and canary plan. oliver — can you spike the coalesce POC next sprint?
oliver: yes, will do a micro-PR on slab manager and run microbenchmarks.
ci-bot: build queued for branch: feature/compaction-adaptive (#3802). tests: unit x72, integration x8.
sara: rollout: canary two non-prod racks 48h, watch p99 and moves/sec.
dave: include kill-switch flags and runbook notes.
anika: i'll draft runbook and dashboards.
sara: thanks team.
